name: kit-notify
description: A sound and a system notification when Claude finishes or needs you, a queue for prompts you type while Claude works (sent one at a time, with a remove button each), and a "while you were away" card when you come back. English and Vietnamese.

sound.title: Play a sound
sound.description: A short sound when Claude finishes a turn that took a while and a different one when it needs you. Plays through the system when it can (macOS, Windows, Linux with PulseAudio, ALSA or libcanberra); where nothing can play, it stays silent.

notify.title: Show a system notification
notify.description: A notification with a title and one line when Claude finishes or needs you, through your terminal's or the app's own notification channel. Where there is none, a short in-app message shows instead.

notifyAfterSec.title: Only notify for turns longer than (seconds)
notifyAfterSec.description: A finished turn notifies (sound and notification) only when it ran at least this many seconds. Needs-you alerts always come. 0 notifies after every turn; a value outside 0 to 3600 is cut to it.

notifyDetails.title: Put the start of Claude's answer in the notification
notifyDetails.description: On: the notification's line is the first line of Claude's last message, or the question it asks. Off: a fixed line that says nothing about your work (useful on a shared screen).

quietHours.title: Quiet hours
quietHours.description: No sound or notification between these local times, for example 22:00-07:00 (it may cross midnight). Empty, the default, means never quiet. A value that is not two times is ignored.

awayMin.title: Welcome-back card after (minutes)
awayMin.description: When you come back after at least this many minutes without typing or sending, and something happened meanwhile, a card sums it up. 0 turns the card off; a value outside 0 to 1440 is cut to it.

showQueueButton.title: Show the "Queue what I typed" button while Claude works
showQueueButton.description: On: while a turn runs and the prompt box holds text, the band offers a button that puts it into the queue (and the button is part of the queue list). Off: only /queue add and the queued list show. The queue itself keeps working.

language.title: Language of the band, card, notifications and /queue
language.description: auto: Vietnamese when Claude Code's own language setting is Vietnamese, English otherwise (looked up once at session start). en: always English. vi: always Vietnamese (Tiếng Việt). What a queued prompt says is sent as you typed it.
